chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subbah al-Kinanee, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man whose wife had divorced him by khula', [asking]: Is it permissible for him to propose marriage to her sister before her waiting period (iddah) expires? He said: 'If her bond of marriage is dissolved and he has not exercised his right of return (raj'ah), then it is permissible for him to propose to her sister.'

key_terms.اِخْتَلَعَتْ: She divorced him (specifically via khula', where the wife initiates divorce often by paying compensation)
key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Right of return / revocation (by the husband during the iddah period)
key_terms.عِصْمَتُهَا: Her bond of marriage / marital tie

ai.seo_question: Can a man propose to his wife's sister before her divorce waiting period ends if the divorce was by khula?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific condition under which a husband may propose to his ex-wife's sister during the *iddah* of a *khula'* divorce: the marriage bond (*'ismah*) must be fully severed, implying no pending *raj'ah* (revocation). This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of *khula'* compared to *talaq*, where the husband retains the right to take back his wife during the waiting period, thereby temporarily prohibiting marriage to her sister. The narration underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the precise timing of legal dissolution in family law.
